what_it_does: C and C++ programs that run on GPUs inherit a classic danger: a bug can cause the program to read or write memory it was never supposed to touch (called an out-of-bounds access), corrupting data or leaking secrets. This paper describes a hardware-plus-compiler system called LMI (Let-Me-In) that prevents such accidents on GPUs. The trick is to hide the allowed size and starting address of each block of memory inside the normally-unused top bits of the pointer (the number the program uses to say 'go look here in memory'), so no extra memory storage is needed. Every time the GPU issues a memory request, dedicated checking hardware compares the address against the embedded limits and blocks any access that falls outside — catching bugs with very little added delay, even when thousands of program threads are running simultaneously. The approach is described as having low overhead even with the GPU's massively parallel nature.
